title: Cyber Insurance Basics for Small Businesses in 2026
description: What small businesses should know before buying cyber insurance: insurer questions, security basics, invoice fraud and breach reporting duties.
h1: Cyber insurance basics for small businesses
intro: Cyber insurance applications ask more about your security than most policies ask about anything. Getting the basics in place makes cover easier to buy and less likely to be needed.

image.alt: Glowing teal LED panel suggesting digital security

sections.html:
• Is multi-factor authentication switched on for email and remote access?
  • Do you take regular backups, stored separately, and have you tested restoring them?
  • Are systems patched and supported?
  • Do staff get phishing awareness training?
  • How do you verify changes to supplier or customer bank details?

In the UK, the NCSC’s Small Business Guide and Cyber Essentials scheme set out the basics. In the US, CISA publishes free resources for small businesses. Working through them helps with insurer questions and reduces risk.

Some of the most common losses involve fake invoices or emails convincing staff to pay into a criminal’s account. Many cyber policies cover this only as an optional extra or with a lower limit. Check the wording, and use call-back checks on known numbers before changing payment details.

Under UK GDPR and EU GDPR, reportable personal data breaches must be notified to the regulator within 72 hours of becoming aware. A good cyber policy gives you fast access to legal and forensic help to meet that deadline. See our cyber insurance guide.

faqs.q: Do sole traders need cyber insurance?
faqs.a: If you hold client data or rely on email and online systems to trade, it’s worth considering. Some policies are designed for very small firms.

faqs.q: Does Cyber Essentials make insurance cheaper?
faqs.a: Some insurers take it into account, and some packages include cyber cover for certified small organisations. Check with insurers.

sources.title: CISA: Cyber guidance for small businesses
